title: SvelteKit 3 Reaches Release Candidate, Moving Config to Vite and Retiring the $lib Alias
gist: SvelteKit 3 reached release candidate as a pruning release: config moves into vite.config.ts, the $lib alias is replaced by Node-native #lib subpath imports, Svelte 5 and Vite 8 with Rolldown become requirements, and remote functions remain experimental.

insights.claim: SvelteKit 3 is in release candidate, framed as a chance to prune older code and lay groundwork rather than a feature-heavy launch, with a stable release expected if testing goes smoothly.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Major JS framework releases are consolidating rather than adding features.
insights.locator: The Svelte team has moved SvelteKit 3

insights.claim: SvelteKit 3 removes svelte.config.js and moves configuration into vite.config.ts so the Vite plugin can read it synchronously instead of waiting for asynchronous resolution.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Deepens framework dependence on Vite as the build-tool standard.
insights.locator: The headline shift is where configuration lives

insights.claim: The most debated change replaces the $lib alias with #lib, using Node's native subpath imports in package.json and requiring file extensions such as #lib/foo.js.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Alignment with platform-native standards reduces framework lock-in for code in lib/server.
insights.locator: The most debated change is the retirement

insights.claim: Rich Harris said he would love everyone to use nodenext but that users might revolt over extensionless imports, adding that opponents can always create their own alias.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Maintainers are weighing standards alignment against developer friction.

insights.claim: SvelteKit 3 requires Vite 8 and its Rolldown bundler for faster builds, but declined to adopt FetchableDevEnvironment, arguing it forces frameworks to absorb too much complexity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Vite/Rolldown are becoming the shared infrastructure layer across front-end frameworks.
insights.locator: Under the hood, SvelteKit 3 now requires Vite 8

insights.claim: SvelteKit 3 requires Svelte 5, enabling improved error handling where +error.svelte renders on load and render failures, all errors go through handleError, and stack traces get sourcemaps.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Forced upgrades accelerate migration to Svelte 5.

insights.claim: Remote functions, a type-safe client-server RPC approach echoing React Server Actions and Next.js server functions, remain experimental, and the team says they make load functions and actions look a bit clunky by comparison.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Svelte is converging on server-function patterns pioneered in the React ecosystem.
insights.locator: Under the hood, SvelteKit 3 now requires Vite 8

insights.claim: SvelteKit is maintained by the Svelte team, now part of Vercel, and positions itself against React frameworks like Next.js and Remix while leaning on Svelte's smaller runtime and reactive syntax.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Vercel backs both Next.js-adjacent and Svelte ecosystems, hedging its front-end framework bets.
insights.locator: SvelteKit is the official application framework
